question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=7 \sin{\left(u \right)},\qquad u=\sin{\left(x - 3 \right)}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=7 \cos{\left(u \right)},\qquad \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\cos{\left(x - 3 \right)}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} &=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\ &=(7 \cos{\left(u \right)})\cdot (\cos{\left(x - 3 \right)}) \\ &=7 \cos{\left(x - 3 \right)} \cos{\left(\sin{\left(x - 3 \right)} \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
f = 5 \cos{\left(u \right)}, \qquad u = \sin{\left(x + 3 \right)} + \frac{5 \pi}{6}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d f}{\textrm d u} = - 5 \sin{\left(u \right)}, \qquad \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} =\cos{\left(x + 3 \right)}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get


$$
\begin{aligned}
 \dfrac{\textrm d f}{\textrm d x} &= \dfrac{\textrm d f}{\textrm d u} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x}\\
&=- 5 \sin{\left(u \right)} \cdot (\cos{\left(x + 3 \right)})\\
&=- 5 \sin{\left(\sin{\left(x + 3 \right)} + \frac{5 \pi}{6} \right)} \cos{\left(x + 3 \right)}.
\end{aligned}

$$

	&=-5 \cdot \frac{1}{2} \\
